recipes.name: Creamy Linguine with Clam Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) can baby clams, drained with juices reserved (such as Bumble Bee®)
1 (16 ounce) jar Alfredo sauce (such as Classico®)
1 teaspoon grated Parmesan cheese, or to taste
1 pinch crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the linguine, and return to a boil. Cook the pasta, stirring occasionally, until cooked through but still slightly firm, about 11 minutes. Drain well.

Heat the butter and olive oil in a skillet over medium heat until it begins to brown slightly. Stir in the onion; cook and stir until the onion becomes lightly golden, about 10 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Add the reserved clam juice and wine. Simmer until reduced by half, about 15 minutes. Stir in the Alfredo sauce and clams; cook and stir until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Serve the clam sauce over the linguine, and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and red pepper flakes.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Linguine with Clam Sauce
raw_recipe.description: White clam sauce is even easier when you use store-bought Alfredo sauce. Extra garlic and onion gives it a great homemade taste.

review.reviewBody: Very very delicious! I have to say the sauce was really good. The combining of clam juice & wine reduction with the alfredo sauce made the ingredients marry so well. It really pulled the clam flavor all the way through the sauce. I thought at first it was going to be really runny but as it turns out, it wasn't. The red pepper flakes gave it a nice heat at the end, but isn't totally neccessary at all, especially with minor children. The only thing I felt that needed more of...was the clams. my cans were 6.5oz cans not 10 oz so for the clams it's self I used 3 cans and only because it look like sauce with a few pieces. And I totally watched how much reserved clam juice I needed because the cans were a total of 13oz, not counting the 3rd can of reserved juice. But however, I'd make this again in a heartbeat. Very well paired with whole grain Linguine noodles. TY grainie.

This was so much better than I expected. My grocery store didn't have whole canned clams - they were either chopped or minced. So instead I bought a bottle of clam juice and a bag of frozen baby clams. I soaked the clams in the clam juice for about an hour so they they both defrosted and got their natural salty flavor back. I used Bertolli Alfredo Sauce with Herbs and used way more than 1 tbsp of wine. I let the juice, wine and veggies cook down to about half before adding the sauce and then added the clams at the last minute so they warmed through but didn't get rubbery. This was absolutely delicious and I will definitely add this to our Christmas seafood dinner this year.

BEST clam sauce I've ever made. I did make a few small adjustments which kicked it up a notch- BACON!!! And mushrooms. Instead of using butter and olive oil, I just fried up about 5 slices of bacon (chopped into pieces before frying). Then added the onions to the bacon grease and bacon pieces, then added fresh mushrooms roughly chopped, then garlic, etc.. Also, I squeezed 1/2 a lemon to the clam juice and wine reduction. The Alfredo sauce is genius and the red pepper flakes add the perfect amount of spice. Phenomenal!!

Tried it your way, but thought the Alfredo Sauce was too overbearing with the clams. The second time I made it, I substituted the Alfredo for same amount of 4% cottage cheese, added some parsley and sliced fresh mushrooms.
Very delicious. Served over a bed of spinach leaves, topped with finely sliced tomato , feta cheese and green onion. I also added a dozen shrimp and 1/4 cup more wine in the sauce.

Delicious, this will be a go to recipe. I used 3 6.5 oz cans of clams and their juice. Sautéd bacon, onions and mushrooms all together and then added 1 T butter and oil the followed the recipe from there forward. It was amazing!
Outstanding. I doubled the crab meat. I cooked the shrimp in a garlic butter sauce. I added a touch of white wine (about 1/4 cup).

I really enjoyed this quick, tasty meal. I used the Classico Alfredo sauce and it was perfect. I only used a dash of the red pepper flakes and added some parsley for some color. I did have to make about 12-14 ounces of pasta to use up all the sauce, 8 oz was not enough in my opinion. Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly, using 3 cans of Snows Chopped Clams, using all the juice from the cans to reduce with the wine. Really good recipe, dare I say restaurant quality? Thanks grainie for the recipe.
I mixed in some imitation crab as well- delicious and easy! Green onion on top too!
Very good with Classico Roasted Garlic Alfredo sauce. I perfer a little morw wine then the recipe calls for though :)
I love this recipe. It is so easy, fast and tastes wonderful. Only changes I made was to leave out the wine and used 2-6.5 oz cans of clams instead of one 10 oz. We will definitly make this again!

Why would one buy Alfredo Sauce especially from Classico, take a read as to what is in it. It is not difficult to prepare an Alfredo Sauce from scratch, much tastier and better. Rest of recipe is very good.
Made this for the first time and will be making again!

I love this recipe! Actually, everyone who eats this love it. I follow the recipe exactly as written. I love love love that the 'reduce by half' includes a time frame. I have made dozens of times. Thank you
Delicious. While family loved it! And easy to make!
Fabulous recipe! I followed one of the comments by adding bacon and mushrooms (still used butter and olive oil). Also added 1/2C frozen peas when the clams went in. Amazing 5 star dish!
Used mushroom Alfredo sauce and it came out delicious!
This recipe made a jar sauce taste very yummy. I will be definitely making this again.
Super easy. Especially after working all day. Really yummy.
Amazing with the clams I also added shrimp
